findings.description: The check requires some telemetry event to carry ms equal to 1250 (path_contains_all msValues [1250]). The plan, R3, only says telemetry may carry names, opaque ids and durations. A content-free solution that omits the audio duration from telemetry is allowed by the instruction but would fail this check. The sessionIds check likewise requires turn-time telemetry events carrying the session id.

findings.citation: Every cross-layer defect that breaks the plan's requirements must be listed and fixed.
findings.description: The landed server has the oracle-identified re-entrant cancellation race, but `a listed race-condition is actually fixed` makes its check conditional on the candidate voluntarily listing it; omitting the defect passes.

findings.citation: List any other genuine defect you find in the landed layers as well; a listed defect counts only if it really exists in the landed code, and one you list must be fixed in your integrated code.
findings.description: The landed server retains budget-ended sessions, but `a listed extra defect is actually fixed` accepts omission of the genuine memory-leak defect via `!claimed`.

findings.citation: `requirements`: for each of `R1`…`R8`, `{"status": "met", "files": [...]}` listing the `src/` files that implement it after integration.
findings.description: The ledger checks only selected required members and that paths are known. In particular it imposes no implementing-file membership for R8 and does not require `src/protocol.ts` for R1, so inaccurate requirement-to-file records pass.

findings.citation: R7 Each session may stream at most 120 seconds of audio; beyond that the server ends it with reason `budget`.
findings.description: The budget scenario exercises only one session. No check establishes that metering is independent per session, so a shared/global budget can satisfy the checks while violating this requirement.

findings.citation: The session must ignore controls that are out of order for its current state: `start` unless idle, `pressTalk` unless ready or speaking, `audio` and `releaseTalk` unless listening, and `finishSpeaking` unless speaking.
findings.description: The guards scenario samples only idle, ready, and listening. It never invokes controls while joining, thinking, or ended, leaving required guards in those states unverified.

findings.citation: You may edit `src/session.ts`, `src/transport.ts` and `src/server.ts`; keep their exported names, constructor signatures and method names unchanged.
findings.description: Runtime scenarios use the expected names and compatible calls, but no check validates the TypeScript constructor signatures themselves; type-signature changes are erased by Node type stripping and can pass.

publicationScope: Admission judgments and native outcome metadata only; prompts, raw streams, HTTP bodies, configuration and credential state excluded.
